prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Context: Meridian region, a dense aviation area. A primary hub, domestic airports and cargo/general aviation aerodromes share terminal airspace. There are two daily demand peaks. Weather (storms, fog, crosswind) reduces the Airport Acceptance Rate. Military/special-use airspace constrains sectors. Surface constraints cover gates, taxi routes, stands and handling. Modes/states: Normal Operations (near capacity), Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase. Mission: a resilient, governed, interoperable air traffic flow management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making (A-CDM) capability that reduces avoidable delay, improves predictability and enables transparent collaboration. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (lead; balances demand vs capacity), Airline Operations Coordinator, Aircraft Operator Representative, Airport Duty Manager, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Slot Coordinator, Military Airspace Liaison. Participating airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Each airport keeps local safety management, certification and command authority. Boundary: the system is a shared coordination layer only. It does not replace ATC, airport control rooms, airline operational control centers or ground handling dispatch (external). System-of-interest: Regional Flow Platform, alias Cedarbell. Components: Demand Prediction Service (estimates demand from schedules, Flight Intent Message, airline recovery plans); Capacity Assessment Module (capacity from weather, runways, sector loading, resources); Slot Allocation Engine (fair, traceable slots); Airport CDM Portal (stakeholders share readiness and confirm decisions); execution elements Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console; data feeds Weather Ingest Gateway, Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Airline Interface Adapter; indicators Sector Load Monitor, Gate Conflict Detector, North Runway Meter, South Runway Meter, East Apron Sensor, West Apron Sensor; Common Situation Display (shared view of demand, capacity, constraints, measures for authorized users); Collaborative Decision Log and Audit Event Ledger (preserve decision rationale, timing, authorization). Requirements: in Adverse Weather Mode or Capacity Reduction State, must support rapid Tactical Regulation Proposal and consistent communication of the Ground Delay Program. In Recovery Phase, must restore flow while monitoring Target Off Block Time, Calculated Takeoff Time and Slot Compliance State.

New part:
S031: Within the boundary, the Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, Slot Allocation Engine, Airport CDM Portal, and Digital Briefing Room support planning and collaborative assessment.
S032: The Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, and Contingency Operations Console support tactical airport and regional coordination.
S033: The Weather Ingest Gateway, Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Airline Interface Adapter, and Alert Distribution Hub provide managed integration points with external systems.
S034: The Performance Analytics Warehouse, Audit Event Ledger, Identity Access Service, Business Rules Registry, and Time Synchronization Service provide governance, security, traceability, and performance measurement capabilities.
S035: The North Runway Meter, South Runway Meter, East Apron Sensor, West Apron Sensor, Sector Load Monitor, and Gate Conflict Detector are treated as connected operational components within the defined technical boundary.
S036: Systems outside the boundary include airline reservation platforms, crew management systems, baggage reconciliation systems, airport commercial systems, national surveillance infrastructure, and aircraft avionics.
S037: Interfaces to external systems are included in the boundary only to the extent required to validate identity, receive authorized operational data, publish approved coordination information, and maintain auditable records.
S038: The Regional Flow Manager is the primary operational role for balancing demand and capacity at the regional level.
S039: The Airline Operations Coordinator, Network Operations Liaison, Aircraft Operator Representative, and Slot Coordinator participate to align airline intentions, schedule constraints, and slot management decisions with the shared plan.
S040: The Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Airport Duty Manager, Ground Handling Dispatcher, and Deicing Coordinator participate to represent local airport, tower, ramp, handling, and winter operations considerations.
S041: The Meteorology Briefing Officer, Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, and Emergency Response Coordinator participate when weather, airspace structure, special-use airspace, or emergency response conditions affect available capacity.
S042: The Data Governance Steward and System Support Engineer participate to maintain data quality, access control, operational continuity, and controlled configuration of the Regional Flow Platform.
S043: Airlines participating in the initial operating concept include scheduled passenger operators, cargo operators, charter operators, and based carriers that require coordinated flow management at the participating airports.
S044: Ground service providers participating in the concept include contracted handlers, fueling providers, deicing providers, towing providers, passenger transport providers, and ramp service organizations operating under airport approval.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
